name: Max Lange Attack
summary: The Max Lange Attack (1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5.O-O Bc5 6.e5) is a sharp gambit that ignites forcing tactics.
intro: The Max Lange Attack arises after 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5.O-O Bc5 6.e5, when White thrusts the e-pawn to strike the f6-knight and rip open the centre. It is one of the most tactical of the Open Games, and can be reached through several move orders, including the Two Knights Defence and the Scotch Gambit.
line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d4 exd4 O-O Bc5 e5

sections.heading: Strategic ideas
paragraphs: White has sacrificed, or at least invested, the d4-pawn to obtain rapid development and open lines, and the advance 6.e5 is the point of the whole system. By attacking the f6-knight while the centre is fluid, White forces Black to react immediately, and the game quickly becomes a race in which accurate calculation matters far more than long-term structure. The bishop on c4 already eyes the sensitive f7-square, and after the centre opens the White pieces flood toward Black’s king before it can find shelter.

Black’s defensive task is to survive the opening storm and reach a position where the extra material tells. The critical continuation runs 6...d5, when Black hits the c4-bishop and tries to blunt White’s initiative by returning some of the tension in the centre. From there the play is heavily forcing, with pins along the e-file, pressure on f7, and tactical motifs against the exposed knights and the black king. If Black threads the needle the queenside majority and sound extra pawn can be decisive, but a single inaccuracy often proves fatal.

sections.heading: Main variations
paragraphs: The main line continues 6...d5, and after 7.exf6 dxc4 8.Re1+ the play revolves around the check on the open e-file and the fate of Black’s king. Black almost always answers 8...Be6, when 9.Ng5 renews the assault against e6 and f7 and forces a long, well-analysed sequence in which both sides walk a tightrope. The resulting positions have been examined move by move for generations, and precise knowledge is essential for either colour.

Sidelines matter too. Instead of 6...d5, the passive 6...Ng4 or 6...Ne4 allow White a strong initiative, and the greedy retreat of the f6-knight without ...d5 usually leaves Black underdeveloped and under fire. Because the Max Lange can be steered into via the Two Knights Defence (after 3...Nf6 4.d4) and the Scotch Gambit, players on both sides must know how the various move orders transpose and where independent try lines diverge.

sections.heading: History and background
paragraphs: The attack is named after the nineteenth-century German master and chess author Max Lange, who examined the 6.e5 advance and helped popularise it. It flourished in the romantic era, when gambit play and direct attacks on f7 were the fashion, and it retains a reputation as one of the sharpest weapons in the Open Games. Modern theory has largely tamed the wildest tries with accurate defence, so the line is seen less often at the highest level, yet it remains a favourite of attacking players and a proving ground for tactical alertness. Its many transpositional paths keep it a practical surprise weapon in club and rapid play.

keyIdeas: 6.e5 hits the f6-knight and opens lines while Black is still developing.
The c4-bishop and open e-file combine to pressure f7 and the black king.
6...d5 is the critical reply, striking the bishop and contesting the centre.
After 7.exf6 dxc4 8.Re1+ Be6 9.Ng5 the play is forcing and heavily theoretical.
Black aims to survive the storm and cash in a sound extra pawn and majority.
Reachable via the Two Knights Defence and Scotch Gambit move orders.

white: Advance e5 to attack the f6-knight and seize the initiative.
Exploit the open e-file with Re1+ and pressure the e6/f7 squares.
Bring the knight to g5 to hammer Black’s pinned and pressured pieces.
Sacrifice material where needed to keep the black king in the centre.
Convert the initiative into a direct mating attack before Black consolidates.
black: Meet 6.e5 with 6...d5 to hit the bishop and challenge the centre.
Block the e-file check with ...Be6 and hold the extra material together.
Untangle the pieces and complete development to weather the assault.
Return material at the right moment to defuse White’s attack.
Exploit the extra pawn and queenside majority once the storm passes.
